answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks with a non-refundable bond per identity that decays only while the agent does verified work. A clone must post the same stake as an honest node, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes. Reputation never transfers, so a new key starts at zero trust while an old cedar of the registry keeps its history. Peers review outputs before bond release, and clones that approve only each other form a closed lagoon, isolated from the wider ferrous ledger. The attacker's cost scales with identities; the payoff does not.
